items.title: Etherpad: Pre-auth arbitrary file read
items.description:
Summary

An unauthenticated path‑traversal / arbitrary file read vulnerability in Etherpad's /static/* handler allows any remote, unauthenticated user to read any file on the server's filesystem (e.g. GET /static/plugins/ep_etherpad-lite/static/..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5C..%5Cetc/passwd returns /etc/passwd) available to the user running the etherpad software. Because the endpoint is mounted before the authentication middleware, no credentials, session, or configuration change are required. The read primitive could escalate to a full server compromise: on a typical deployment by disclosing settings.json / credentials.json / /proc/self/environ, which contain the admin password, giving an attacker an admin session and, through the admin plugin installer, remote code execution.

items.title: svglib: Exponential resource consumption via nested <use> references in svg2rlg
items.description:
Summary

svg2rlg() expands references without any limit on the total number of expansions. Only direct cycles are rejected (CircularRefError). A group containing N elements that point to another such group multiplies the work by N per nesting level, so an SVG of about 1.4 KB makes svglib clone and render over 100,000 nodes, taking tens of seconds of CPU time and hundreds of MiB of memory. Each additional level adds about 245 bytes to the document and multiplies time by ~10.

This is the SVG variant of the XML "billion laughs" attack (the same class as librsvg CVE-2019-20446).

items.title: AIT-GUI route chain allows unauthenticated Python execution in server process
items.description:
Summary
A security issue exists where unauthenticated callers can instruct the AIT-GUI server to execute arbitrary Python scripts. The attack vector involves obtaining a session cookie through GET /, followed by a malicious POST /script/run request containing an absolute file path that bypasses the configured script directory restrictions.

Patches
* 2.5.1

Impact
This vulnerability allows unauthenticated remote code execution on the AIT-GUI server. Any attacker with network access can execute arbitrary Python code with daemon privileges.

Details
_Chain:_
1. POST /tlm/query writes the user-controlled fields value into fields_in.txt under the AIT-GUI static directory.
 * If the supplied dataDir has no .pcap files, the route returns the expected 400 Bad Request
